content:
@Håkan Svensson @Douwe Fokkema @TwoCan @Dave Register @Pavel Kalian

We have some inconsistencies when configuring n2k interfaces

  • N2k over TCP/UDP and regular serial connections does have checkboxes enabling input and/or output; N2k over socketcan and slcan does not have such checkboxes
  • The "is driver output capable" is used to govern whether the autopilot pgns should be sent. socketcan/slcan are hardcoded as in/out and have no possibility to disable this.
  • For N0183, all connections have the enable input/output checkboxes, the output checkbox overloaded with sending autopilot info
  • Plugins scans the available drivers for those are marked as being capable of output and uses this/these sending data.

Together, a considerable mess. @TwoCan and I have discussed this, and for n2k we think that:

  1. All n2k connections are bidirectional, being capable of both input and output. There is thus no need for "enable input/output " checkboxes for n2k connections.
  2. OTOH, a checkbox for "send autopilot info" is required.

For n0183, things are perhaps more complicated. First question becomes if we actually have n0183 connections which are physically output or input only. Such wiring is certainly possible, but is it actually used?

That is, would it be OK to simplify 0183 connections like for n2k above? Hardcoded input + output, a separate "Send autopilot info" checkbox?

Thoughts?

A N0183 connection is not like a N2k bus, i.e. a single data wire. We have one RX and one TX and they can be used to connect one or more devices. It's for example rather common to get RX from a GNSS receiver and the TX for the same RS232/USB-connection wired to a AP. Not less it's a way to save serial-USB converters. So the answer to "Such wiring is certainly possible, but is it actually used?" is "Yes".

OK, new iteration. First n2k connections

  • No input/output checkboxes, n2k is always bidirectional.
  • New checkbox "Send autopilot /NMEA repeater info" which governs if PGN 129283, 129284, 12928 are sent on the wire

For 0183 connections:

  • Two checkboxes for enabling input/output. Mostly like today but:
  • New checkbox "Send autopilot /NMEA repeater info" which governs sending of APB, RMB, RMC, XTE. Invalid if "Enable output" is not checked.

All this will need a new flag in ConnectionParams, and updates to code sending the autopilot info.

Thoughts on this?

Even in Hakan's scenario, It is still a bi-directional connection, no need to have checkboxes to enable input or output. OpenCPN, neither knows nor cares that the Tx & Rx pins are connected to different devices.

The question is what happens if either the serial Rx or Tx wires are not connected ? From a software perspective, nothing.
Well. if we have n0183 connection not capable of output plugins will find and use this driver unless it is marked input-only. Or?

OpenCPN and Plugins still have no way of knowing whether something is physically connected to the end of the Tx pin.
For example, just because OpenCPN sends NMEA 0183 APB, RMB & XTE sentences, or WMM Plugin sends a magnetic variation sentence, there is no acknowledgement it was sent, as far as the UART is concerned, the signal was sent, the electricity just dissipates into the ether.
Indeed. But assuming there are two connections, just one of which usable and a clever user it is possible to manually configure the drivers so plugins can do the right choice.
... that is, if the input/output checkboxes exist.

New checkbox "Send autopilot /NMEA repeater info"

So you mean that can be used as today's output but a filter is already prepared?
In the case I don't want all ECxxx it can be tricky.
I think it can be confusing with two different outputs for N0183. Keep it to the one we have today. But to serve the user the ECxxx idea can be adapted by a checkbox for the serial output to add the AP (ECxxx) filter while the connection is created. But that filter must, as usual, be able to edit afterwards.
Steven I think we still need both for the serial connection. What we could need is a logic to hinder echoing all data to the output. Or.. simply: No checkbox for AP-sentences as I wrote above but instead the AP filter for a new serial output all time. If the user want another filter he can edit the default. Then we have minimized the risk for feedback.
Also bear in mind the "Send to GPS" function who to some extent evade the rules in connections.

So you mean that can be used as today's output but a filter is already prepared?

No. Today, the multiplexer checks the connection direction setting. If it is input + output or just output it sends the autopilot messages for n2k or 0183 depending on connection.

The problem with this scheme is that there is no way to configure a connection to handle output without also getting the autopilot info. This is an obvious mistake, being able to send output is one thing, to want the autopilot info another. This is clearly visible for n2k, but 0183 is actually the same. Nothing of this is related to filters
BTW: this path includes migration stuff :(
I don't understand... If I have a serial output wired to a AP I of course use a filter today. Basically only send ECxxx or list the one I want.

Perhaps your use case is not the universal one applying to everyone. :)

Perhaps it's not wired to an AP at all, but still wants output sent by a plugin?

The filters don't change.

The question for plugins is how do they detect which connection to use? Today if there are multiple bi-directional connections, either the plugin prompts the user to select one, it uses an arbitrary connection (eg. the first) or it uses all.

The next question is how many plugins actually use WriteCommDriver ? A quick search of Rick's repo, only one, the VDR plugin. From what a quick search revealed, none of Mike's.

The WMM plugin still uses PushNMEABuffer which if I understand correctly has no notion of In/Out ?

Douwe's (and I think Bernd's) plugins are all N2K. Sean's PyPilot ? Doesn't it talk TCP/IP to the PyPilot controller?
The exampled user case to send to an AP is clearly described in the manual and frequently used.

The exampled user case to send to an AP is clearly described in the manual and frequently used.

This use case doesn't change.

I see no need for to change the serial in/out function apart from the security feature to add the "Send only the ECxxx"
For N2k you have the best experiences.
Now late and I've to quit for today. See you...

The question for plugins is how do they detect which connection to use? Today if there are multiple bi-directional connections, either the plugin prompts the user to select one, it uses an arbitrary connection (eg. the first) or it uses all.

yes. But if only one is configured as bidirectional (or output only) this selection is done. This is a reason for keeping the enable input/output checkboxes for n0183. It doesn't solve all problems, but some.

The WMM plugin still uses PushNMEABuffer

PushNMEABuffer is about distributing messages on the internal bus and plugin callbacks. It is not about sending on the wire.

Huh? PushNMEABuffer does go onto the wire if there are outbound NMEA 0183 connections.

OK, if you want to avoid potentially breaking stuff, then probably safer to leave NMEA 0183 the way it is.
There are times when telemetry would be useful, so you could actually find out how OpenCPN is being used & configured.

uh? PushNMEABuffer does go onto the wire if there are outbound NMEA 0183 connections

This is about something listening to the internal bus and forwarding it to drivers (no, the details are lost in my limited memory). The point is that anything sending on the wire will have to use either the plugin interface or the drivers directly, and there is direction checking in both cases

Don't ruin the amazing multiplexer we have in OCPN. PushNMEABuffer sends to the multiplexer and what appears there can be forwarded to every N0183 output connection. A fantastic feature, but filters must be used almost all the time. The multiplexer's data is also often used via UDP and wifi to share all Nav data with other OCPNs onboard. PC and Android.

Q about N2k output.
Now when we navigate an active route the AP-data (ECxxx and corresponding PGNs) are sent out by any N2k connection. Is there a need for an enable/disable option to avoid the risk of data colliding with other onboard systems?
Or is it as simple as if you have other systems, a route in OCPN is not activated? (>> KISS)

Is there a need for an enable/disable option to avoid the risk of data colliding with other onboard systems?

This is the starting point for this discussion. The answer is yes.

Which leads to a n2k connection setup with this single checkbox "Send AP/repeater data". It is not related to enable input/enable output. n2k is always bidirectional. Seems clarified for n2k for me..

Now, with this separate "Send AP/repeater data" setting being introduced to all n2k connections, the question becomes why it should not work the same way also for 0183

For N0183 we need both the In/Out-put selections.
To facilitate the user we may, as discussed above, add a "send only EC"-filter button that in some way add the appropriate filter.
But a info-dialog how to add that filter might be as good?

Is there a need for an enable/disable option to avoid the risk of data colliding with other onboard systems?

Not really.

Transmitting PGN's 129283, 129284 and 129285 enables two things.

  1. It allows instruments displays and MFD's to display the current route and waypoint information (bearing and range to waypoint, cross track error, time to go), no different to the little widget displayed in OpenCPN when a waypoint or route is activated.
  2. When a NMEA 2000 autopilot is in Nav mode, it supplies the necessary data for the autopilot to adjust the course.
    The presence of these PGN's generated by OpenCPN does not cause the autopilot to switch from standby to nav mode, this is performed by manufacturer proprietary PGN's. It does not cause a MFD to activate a route and begin generating its own PGN's.

The only risk is if a sailor manually activates a route on both OpenCPN and a MFD. Both will generate these PGN's and two sets of conflicting PGN's may "confuse" an autopilot, or cause instrument displays to display different values. Or if the user activates a route on two different instances of OpenCPN. We cannot defend against stupidity.

As NMEA 2000 is bi-directional, removing the In/Out checkboxes should be a no brainer. One could make the case, that if PGN filtering was available for NMEA 2000, you don't even need a checkbox for "Send Navigation Data", you would just need to configure PGN's 129283, 129284 & 129285 to be accepted in the outbound filter.

An interesting thought, is to enable plugins to alter the filter. For example, the WMM plugin needs to transmit PGN 127258, the plugin should be able to add that to the list, rather than relying on the user to add the entry.

But this maybe unnecessary as in the normal use case the filter list could be empty (transmit everything) because only data that is written to CommDriverN2K gets transmitted.

I can't see any reason why the same design cannot be used for NMEA 0183. As I said, OpenCPN neither knows, nor cares whether the physical NMEA 0183 Tx connection is electrically connected to something.

Again, it doesn't need a specific checkbox to "send navigation data to an autopilot", a user just needs to enable APB, RMB and XTE sentences, whether they are prefixed with the "EC" talker Id, is unimportant. Here the filter list is important because there are two interfaces/API's, PushNMEABuffer and WriteCommDriver which behave slightly differently.

This is an opportunity to simplify the UI and make it consistent.

N2k: KISS. that is. WE must assume the user know what he is doing.

N0183: re:"enable APB, RMB and XTE sentences, whether they are prefixed with the "EC" talker Id, is unimportant." Not really. RMB can come from several sources, even those that are deprioritized. An AP usually only wants ECRMB.
Otherwise I agree

Without a literature review, I would suggest that most autopilots would accept any valid talkerId, EC (Electronic Chart), GP (GPS System) or II (Integrated Instrumentation), but perhaps safer to leave ECAPB, ECRMB, ECXTE as defaults in the NMEA 0183 filter list.

Was the selection of EC just a historical artifact chosen by Dave because EC (Electronic Chart) seemed apt for OpenCPN?

The Talker is not for the AP. Either works as usual.
The "EC" talker for this filter is internal OCPN. It is most likely created by autopilot_output.cpp and nothing else. That's why.

OK, I misunderstood your earlier comment. As I surmised, from an autopilot's perspective, the talker Id is unimportant. The EC talkerId is generated internally by OpenCPN, and the default can be changed using the connections dialog.

We need to sort this out. Let's try to start with n2k: Questions:

  1. Should all n2k connections be similar w r t enable/input output and sending AP data? Tentative answer: yes
  2. Should n2k connections have enable input/output checkboxes? Tentative answer: no
  3. Should n2k connections have a "Send AP/Repeater info" checkbox? Tentative answer: yes.

What can we agree on here?

With my limited N2k knowledge, I have no objections.
One question: How does OCPN respond to a request about what kind of system this is? I suppose we must send some form of identity PGN, which means forced function for output?
Since we are about to hardcode n2k connection as bidirectional this is not an issue, right?
No issue, agree.
So now we need @TwoCan 's input before we proceed

Overall yes, but a couple of nuanced points.

Should all n2k connections be similar w r t enable/input output and sending AP data?

Without delving into the code, it may be possible for OpenCPN and auto-detect to inadvertently use an Actisense protocol that may not be supported for both Receive and Transmit with a specific gateway.

For example on the Actisense W2K-2, WGX-1 and W2K-1, both ASCII Raw and Actisense Raw are not supported for Receive or Transmit on either TCP or UDP. However on the NGX-1 (USB), both N2K ASCII and ASCII Raw are Receive only.

What this really means is that depending on the gateway, some protocols cannot be considered to be bi-directional. We don't have the ability for the user to configure a protocol, we currently rely on auto-detect.

  1. Should n2k connections have a "Send AP/Repeater info" checkbox? Tentative answer: yes.

Assuming core OpenCPN always generates PGN's 129283, 129284 and 129285 when a waypoint or route is active and that this checkbox merely filters these PGN's from the connection, then in the absence of a NMEA 2000 filter, this is the only solution.

Later if an output filter capability was added, then this checkbox could be omitted and the guidance to the user to would be to configure a filter to accept or refuse the navigation PGN's, in a similar way that setting a filter for APB, RMB and XTE sentences for NMEA 0183 connections is done today.

TLDR: Yes, in agreement.

OK, all agree so far.

Now to 0183. First question is if there should be "Enable input" and "Enable output" checkboxes. Note that this is not about sending AP/repeater info or not, lets postpone that discussion. So:

  1. Should 0183 connections have "Enable input" and "Enable output" checkboxes? Tentative answer: yes.

Can we agree on this?

No, I don't agree.
Why do we need them ?
For a serial port, If the Rx or Tx pins are not connected (ie. open circuit), nothing bad will happen.

And for the case that Hakan mentioned, where Rx might be connected to a GPS and Tx to an autopilot, this fits perfectly well.

For network ports, keep in mind that it also depends on whether the user has configured their gateway to be uni-directional (Rx or Tx) or bi-directional. But I can't see any problem if a connection "receives nothing" or transmits something but no-one else is listening.

My only concern is that I don't know what these settings have on the internal plumbing. Does the enable output checkbox toggle the behaviour for generating APB, RMB and XTE sentences, or will they always be generated ?

From a plugin perspective like WMM, if NMEA 0183 by default is bi-directional, but the user does not want magnetic variation transmitted, they just need to configure an outbound filter.

I can't see any harm in NMEA 0183 being bi-directional.
